{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows positive sentiment (e.g., >0.00) and model overestimates prices, indicating bullish sentiment may be overblown.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude when recent history shows strong upward momentum followed by a sharp drop — model tends to overreact to recent spikes.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-10 day average, reduce by 5-10% to avoid over-optimism.",
    "When sentiment history includes a 0.33 or higher value, slightly increase forecast downward to reflect cautious market behavior.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, reduce forecast by 3-5% if true outcome is consistently below model, indicating model is overconfident in upward trends.",
    "If model forecast is above 70.00 and true outcome is below 65.00, apply a 5-10% downward correction to avoid overestimating upside potential.",
    "When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model should not overreact — apply a conservative correction to avoid false peaks.",
    "For forecasts with high volatility (e.g., >10% deviation from true outcome), apply a smoothing filter to reduce noise and avoid erratic swings."
  ]
}
